findings.title: Feature-flagged table widget renders empty data for every table
findings.body: When the `use-table-widget-visualization` feature is enabled, this branch replaces the populated `SimpleTableChart` with `TableWidgetVisualization` initialized with `columns={[]}` and a hard-coded `tableData` containing no rows and empty meta. It never passes `result.data`, `result.meta`, the result title, loading state, or custom field renderers, so every dashboard table widget becomes blank for organizations with the flag on. The new visualization needs to receive the actual `result` data, or the branch must remain disabled until that integration is implemented.

findings.title: Error details can be paired with the wrong replay error IDs
findings.body: `fetch_error_details` builds `node_ids` from `error_ids` and then does `zip(error_ids, events.values())`. `nodestore.backend.get_multi` returns a mapping keyed by node ID and can omit missing nodes; its value ordering is also not guaranteed to match the input list. If any event is missing or the backend returns a different order, the `zip` shifts entries: an error ID is paired with another event's title/message/timestamp, causing incorrect error context in the replay AI summary. Iterate `events.items()` and derive the event ID from the node key, or build a `node_id -> event_id` mapping and look up each result explicitly.

findings.title: Timestamp/age mutual exclusion ignores zero values and neither is required
findings.body: `validate_timestamp` and `validate_age` check the other field via truthiness (`self.initial_data.get("age")` / `get("timestamp")`). Since zero is a valid value for these integer fields, a report containing `timestamp` and `age: 0` (or `age` and `timestamp: 0`) passes validation even though the two fields are supposed to be mutually exclusive. Both fields are also optional, so a report with neither timestamp nor age is accepted, whereas the old structure required a timestamp. Use key-presence checks and enforce that exactly one of the two fields is supplied.

findings.title: PR comment helpers are placed on CommitContextIntegration but used from PRCommentWorkflow
findings.body: `get_merged_pr_single_issue_template` calls `PRCommentWorkflow._truncate_title(title)`, but `_truncate_title` is defined on `CommitContextIntegration`. The new helpers are invoked from `GitHubPRCommentWorkflow`/`GitlabPRCommentWorkflow` via `self.get_environment_info` and `self.get_merged_pr_single_issue_template`; those workflows derive from `PRCommentWorkflow`, not from `CommitContextIntegration`, so these methods are not available on `self`. This will raise `AttributeError` when building a merged PR comment. Move the helpers onto `PRCommentWorkflow` (or call them through the integration object) and reference the defining class consistently.

findings.title: Hook can return undefined attributes when the query is disabled or has no data
findings.body: The new `useQuery` return path exposes `data` directly as `attributes`. When `enabled` is false, or before a successful fetch, `data` is `undefined`; the previous implementation always built and returned a `TagCollection` object (falling back to `{}` over `result.data ?? []`). Consumers that spread or iterate `attributes` can now throw. Return a safe default such as `attributes: isFetching ? previous ?? {} : data ?? {}`.

findings.title: New None max_segment_id handling is not actually exercised by this test
findings.body: This test changes the mocked row to `max_segment_id: None`, but `delete_matched_rows` is mocked, so the new `_make_recording_filenames` branch (`if row["max_segment_id"] is None: return []`) is never called. The production fix in `src/sentry/replays/usecases/delete.py` remains untested. Add a test that calls `delete_matched_rows` with a real row or directly calls `_make_recording_filenames` and asserts it returns no filenames for a null segment ID.
